Ibrahim A: quick experiment results for orion14b (14B) using adaptive-prefix cache + int6 default, fall back int8 on cache-miss / long inputs. 8k webchat sample. TL;DR: net cost down ~26% with cache hit=31%; QA down small (~1.1pp) but hallucination concentrated on low-repeat prompts.

Nina V: interesting. what's the cache design and numbers?

Ibrahim A: cache = prefix-based LRU at request-granularity using embedding-fingerprint (cosine>0.98). TTL=24h. cache_hit_rate=31% on trace; when hit we serve cached token stream (int6) -> huge token savings.

eval-bot: summary: sample_n=8000, overall_cost_delta=-26% vs all-int8, cache_hit=31%, qa_acc_delta=-1.1pp, hallucination_delta=+1.7pp concentrated on non-repeated abstractive prompts, p95_latency_delta=-8ms, avg_tokens_saved_per_req=420

Carlos M: paste the table pls.

Ibrahim A: small table:
```
variant                cost_per_1k  QA_acc  halluc_rate  p95_latency  notes
orion14b-int8-baseline $0.92        84.2%   2.4%         240ms        all-int8
orion14b-int6+cache    $0.68        83.1%   4.1%         232ms        int6 default + prefix cache
```

Sophie: +1 on cost but halluc goes up on low-repeat prompts. any mitigations?

Ibrahim A: mitigations tested: 1) cache-threshold increase (cosine>0.995) -> hit_rate down to 18% but halluc delta -> +0.6pp; 2) cache-stale-check: re-score top-1 token logits with int8 on cache-miss -> extra cost +4% but reduces halluc by ~1.1pp; 3) route >1500 tokens to int8 directly.

Nina V: what about routing hybrid + cache? e.g., cache only for short flows and route long contexts to int8?

Ibrahim A: ran that sim: policy = "if tokens>1500 -> int8; else if cache_hit -> serve cached int6; else int6". Result: effective cost ~-21% vs all-int8, hallucination delta ~+0.9pp. Good compromise.

Ibrahim A: sim command we used:
```bash
python tools/sim_cache_routing.py \
  --trace traces/webchat_8k.json \
  --cache-config "threshold=0.98,ttl=86400" \
  --policy "len>1500->int8;cache_hit->int6;else->int6" \
  --metrics cost,qa_acc,halluc_rate,p95,hit_rate \
  --out reports/orion14b_cache_3776543210.json
```

Carlos M: unit-econ for GTN please (assume avg tokens/req=1.2k).

Ibrahim A: quick calc:
- baseline all-int8: cost_per_1k=$0.92 -> cost_per_req ~= $1.10 -> per_1M_req ~= $1,100
- cache+int6 hybrid (31% hit): effective cost_per_1k~$0.68 -> cost_per_req ~= $0.81 -> per_1M_req ~= $810
- savings ~= $290 per 1M requests (~26.4%)

Sophie: that's compelling. product question: recommended rollout and guardrails?

Nina V: propose: canary 3% -> 20% over 10 days. Gates: hallucination_rate (>4% absolute), QA_slice_delta (>2pp on priority slices), cache_hit_rate (should not drop >10% from sim), p95 latency. Fallback: revert to all-int8 routing or tighten cache threshold.

Ibrahim A: caveats: numbers assume repeat traffic and current priming. heavy personalization or ephemeral prompts reduce cache effectiveness. also extra infra for cache storage + consistency.

Carlos M: ops items: add billing tags per-variant, expose cache_hit_rate metric, add alert if hallucination >4% for 5m or hit_rate <15% sustained 10m. Also need a small smoke harness to validate cache correctness on canary.

Sophie: can someone draft a one-paragraph exec blurb + the unit econ numbers for GTN?

Ibrahim A: draft exec blurb: "Recommend piloting an adaptive-prefix cache with int6 default and int8 fallback for long contexts. In simulation this hybrid reduced model spend by ~26% while keeping most short-flow quality within 1pp of baseline; we observed hallucination increases on low-repeat abstractive prompts which are manageable via threshold tuning or selective int8 re-score. Start with a 3% canary and expand to 20% on success with gates for hallucination, QA-slice regression, and cache hit-rate. Implement billing tags and a revert-to-int8 fallback if guardrails trip."
